consts.name: degMaximCount
consts.comment: the maxim roster count: seven basic principles for running a high-level campaign - don't depend on the dice, use adversaries intelligently and inventively, control magic, be aware of demographics, think on an epic scale, plan ahead, share responsibility with the players.

consts.name: degHighLevelFloor
consts.comment: the high-level definition: for this book's purposes, any character of level 10 or more is high-level (printed p. 6).

consts.name: degBookLevelCap
consts.comment: the book's scope: rules and campaign suggestions for characters of up to 30th level (printed p. 6) - the ceiling the Chapter 7 ascension doctrine later caps.

consts.name: degRetirementLevel
consts.comment: the retirement frame: per the DMG Chapter Three, retirement is inevitable once characters exceed level 20 - the doctrine this book argues against (printed p. 6).

consts.name: degFlatXpFrom
consts.comment: the beyond-9th-level breakdown: the experience required to gain the next level no longer increases geometrically once the PCs reach 9th level - a flat increase from level to level instead (printed p. 8, Figure 3).

consts.name: degDemographicTenth
consts.comment: the demographic ladder, Table 1: there is only one 10th-level character in a general population of 5,000 (printed p. 22).

consts.name: degDemographicEighteenth
consts.comment: the demographic ladder's top: an 18th-level character of any class is truly a one-in-a-million individual (printed p. 22).

consts.name: degPaladinRate
consts.comment: the subclass rarity: only .2% of the population (1 in 500) qualifies to be a paladin; other subclasses with strict ability requirements (bards, rangers, druids) are equally rare (printed p. 22).

bools.name: degMaximRoster
bools.comment: the seven named maxims, in book order: don't depend on the dice; use adversaries intelligently and inventively; control magic; be aware of demographics; think on an epic scale; plan ahead; share responsibility with your players - following them does not guarantee a great game, but all successful high-level campaigns use them to one degree or another.

bools.name: degForewordDweomerThesis
bools.comment: the foreword preview, Chapter 6: true dweomers are essentially 10th-level spells - world-shaking magic for high-level spellcasters, included to allow the casting of a single true dweomer to keep a group of PCs busy for a long time.

bools.name: degForewordAutoFail
bools.comment: the foreword preview, Chapter 7: the revised rule for automatic failure of saving throws - something that places a little fear back into high-level characters' lives.

bools.name: degTensionDoctrine
bools.comment: the first maxim's core: maintain tension without inflating the level of power - create situations where the players rely on their own memories and reasoning skills; not every encounter has to be a fight; do not allow the PCs to become so dominant that every situation descends into a die-rolling extravaganza.

bools.name: degEpicScaleDoctrine
bools.comment: the fifth maxim's core: heroes are not anonymous, heroes deserve heroic tasks, and the impact of high-level deeds reaches far - the campaign doctrine of printed pp. 22-23.
